title: Pointed etale witness for equality of inverse-image unit sections
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], and write $b_i$ for base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and $i^*F$ for the constructed sheaf pullback with unit $\eta$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. For objects $W\to X$ and $V\to Z$ of the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], a $Z$-morphism $f:V\to b_i(W)$, a point $z\in V$, and sections $s,t\in F(W)$, suppose $(i^*F)(f)(\eta_W(s))=(i^*F)(f)(\eta_W(t))$. Then there exist an object $U\to X$ of the small etale site, an $X$-morphism $g:U\to W$, and $u\in U$ whose image in $X$ is $i(V\to Z)(z)$, such that $F(g)(s)=F(g)(t)$. The universe of section sets is at least the universe of the site.

proof.text: Unfold the constructed pullback adjunction unit: it is the left Kan extension unit followed by the sheafification unit. Naturality of the latter rewrites the assumed equality as equality of sheafification images of two Kan-extension sections indexed by (W,f).

proof.text: Prove local injectivity of the sheafification unit in the specified universe. For the plus construction, equality of two constant matching-family representatives is equality after a common refinement (GrothendieckTopology.Plus.eq_mk_iff_exists). That refinement is a covering sieve of arrows on which the sections agree. Apply this to both plus operations; local injectivity is closed under composition. The natural isomorphism from plus-plus to the chosen sheafification identifies their units, and postcomposition by an isomorphism preserves local injectivity. Thus the equalizer sieve of the two Kan-extension sections is covering.

proof.text: The equality in the sheaf pullback is equality of sheafification images of the two presheaf coprojections indexed by (W,f). Local injectivity of sheafification gives a covering sieve where these coprojections restrict equally. Use the small etale covering criterion to choose an arrow Vprime to V and a point above z. The restricted coprojections have the same index (W, f composed with Vprime to V). Filtered-colimit eventual equality supplies one index U receiving an arrow from this common index in the opposite category, with equal restrictions of s,t. Opposing gives g:U to W and a map Vprime to U times_X Z. Project the chosen point to U; the commuting pullback square identifies its image with i(V.hom(z)).

lean.statement:
theorem etale_pullback_unit_pointed_witness
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (W : X.Etale) (V : Z.Etale)
    (f : V ⟶ (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i).obj W)
    (z : V.left) (s t : F.obj.obj (op W))
    (heq :
      ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
        (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i) (Type (max (u + 1) v))
        (X.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
        (Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).obj F).obj.map f.op
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
          (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i) (Type (max (u + 1) v))
          (X.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
          (Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app F).hom.app (op W) s) =
      ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
        (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i) (Type (max (u + 1) v))
        (X.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
        (Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).obj F).obj.map f.op
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
          (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i) (Type (max (u + 1) v))
          (X.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
          (Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app F).hom.app (op W) t)) :
    ∃ (U : X.Etale) (g : U ⟶ W) (u : U.left),
      U.hom u = i (V.hom z) ∧ F.obj.map g.op s = F.obj.map g.op t
